quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 20 Questions • Passing Score 16

questions.question: At night, should you follow other vehicles more closely or farther away than during the day?

options.text: Keep the same distance day or night.

questions.explanation: It is hard to see distances in the dark. You cannot see shadows or light changes that help you judge distance during the day. Stay farther back when riding at night than you do during the day.

questions.question: You should check your motorcycle before riding because:

options.text: Only a mechanic can do a useful check.
You should not check it before a ride.
You should only check it after a ride.
It can find mechanical problems or broken equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can find mechanical problems or broken equipment.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This helps you find problems that could hurt you or cause your bike to break down.

questions.question: When you make eye contact with another driver:

options.text: You know for sure they see you.
It is not worth your time.
It does not mean they will let you go when they should.
They will always let you go.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will let you go when they should.
questions.explanation: Do not assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers sometimes look right at a motorcycle but do not see it.

questions.question: A passenger should:

options.text: Lean when you lean through turns.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when you lean through turns.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to lean with you during turns and curves. They should hold your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head to check your blind spot.
Point in the direction you are turning.
Speed up to pass other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Do not only trust your mirrors.

questions.question: To stop quickly, what should you do?

options.text: Slow the engine and use the front brake.

questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: Where is the throttle on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Know where all your controls are before you ride.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: If you need to stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear is also called:
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle like braking does. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: The gearshift lever is operated with:
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest and is operated by your left foot.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery road, what should you do?

options.text: Lean into the slippery section to stay balanced.
Keep your speed up to improve traction.
Do not worry about the road conditions.
Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.
questions.explanation: It is best to avoid slippery roads entirely. If you cannot avoid one, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: What type of footwear is best for riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Sturdy boots or high shoes that support your ankles provide the best protection. Laced boots are best. If your boots have long laces, tuck them in securely before riding.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT help reduce your chance of a crash?

options.text: Be ready to react to hazards.

questions.explanation: To avoid a crash, be visible to other riders. Signal your plans clearly. Keep space between you and other vehicles. Watch ahead for hazards and be ready to react.

questions.question: What should you do with a motorcycle helmet after a crash?
questions.explanation: Always replace a helmet after a crash.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can affect a rider's ability to ride?
questions.explanation: Just one alcoholic drink can affect your ability to ride. It is illegal and dangerous to ride a motorcycle after drinking alcohol.

questions.question: Where is the gear shift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest. Use your left foot to operate it. Push up to shift to a higher gear. Push down to shift to a lower gear.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when preparing to pass a vehicle on its left?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center portion of your lane.
Try to stand up on your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass on the left. This gives you a better view of the road ahead and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What should NOT be checked in your pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Check tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn before every ride. Do this inspection before mounting your motorcycle.

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Stay seated and lift your feet from the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down. Approach it at a 90-degree angle if you can. Keep your motorcycle straight. Just before hitting it, ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever usually located?
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is usually located on the left handgrip of a motorcycle.
